story: Shukracharya, guru of the asuras, knew the Mritasanjivani, a secret mantra that could bring the dead back to life. He used it to revive the asuras in their wars with the gods, and advised kings like Mahabali.
belief: He is honoured as a great sage and as the planet Venus, Shukra, after whom Friday, Shukravar, is named. The Shukra Niti, a text on politics, is attributed to him.
turns: To stop Mahabali's gift to Vamana, he blocked the spout of the water pot used to seal it. Vamana poked the spout with a blade of grass and blinded him in one eye. His loyalty kept him serving the asuras even when they were wrong.
facts: He is the planet Venus in Indian astrology.
His daughter Devayani married King Yayati.
Kacha, son of his rival Brihaspati, came as his student and learned the Mritasanjivani.
lessons: Knowledge is only as good as the cause it serves.
Standing by the underdog is noble, but check the cause.
more: He lost an eye to the blade of grass Vamana poked into the water pot.
He is the guru of the asuras just as Brihaspati is the guru of the gods.
